frontier.hypothesis: The permuter modality is now measured exhausted for this function at the h2a base — the remaining lever is a DIFFERENT BASE, not a different search. Re-seed a cheat-suppressed campaign from the s2 h1d chassis (floor 10, shared complete_store WITHOUT the per-arm var_v1 staging) so the search starts in a different basin than the h2a local minimum s5 just proved strict.
frontier.mechanism: s5 proved h2a is a strict local minimum under legitimate mutation, and the permuter score is a faithful gradient here (235 == 2 insns + 7 regs). A local minimum is basin-relative: h1d differs from h2a by the staging construct itself, so its legitimate-mutation neighborhood is disjoint from the one s5 exhausted. Re-running chassis A's weights from h1d costs one campaign and either finds a different descent path or converts 'h2a is a local min' into 'the whole region is'.

frontier.hypothesis: The 2-instruction shortfall is a delay-slot FILL-PRIORITY decision inside reorg.c fill_slots_from_thread that no expression-level or whole-case-body respelling reaches; the deciding input is the liveness of $v0 across the branch, which is set by what the SECOND switch(idx) and the func_8005C650 call do with $v0 — i.e. the lever may be OUTSIDE the switch(ret) region entirely.
frontier.mechanism: s5 exhaustively swept every legitimate spelling and whole-case structure INSIDE the switch(ret) region and the score never moved off 235. reorg.c picks the fall-through fill over the dead-branch fill based on cost plus register liveness on the opposite thread. The liveness of $v0 at the branch is determined by the code AFTER do_call (the jal to func_8005C650 and the idx = (D_800A34F8 >> 13) & 7 reload), which every s1-s5 probe left untouched. A forensics session reading the .greg / reorg dumps would identify which register's liveness flips the choice.
